# Five-minute demo script

Use the deployed visualizer to demonstrate one student decision: which AI direction and skill to explore next.

## 0:00-0:35 - Frame the sample
Open Opportunity landscape. Say: this is a dated, source-backed sample of 852 public US AI postings from 107 companies. It describes the observed sample, not the entire labor market.

## 0:35-1:25 - Set the shared filters
Use primary role direction, experience level, US region/state/remote, and graduate evidence. Start with All, then choose one direction and Explicit graduate. Point out that all charts update to the selected sample. Reset graduate evidence to All before exploring skills.

## 1:25-2:20 - Read Opportunity landscape
Show distributions by direction, experience, and region. Explain that state totals can overlap when one posting lists multiple places. Use the skill-demand matrix to answer which skills are mentioned across directions. This is mention coverage, not proficiency or eligibility.

## 2:20-3:55 - Run Skill lab
Open Skill lab directly. Select local-only skill chips, optionally turn on Remember on this device, and show the fraction and count of filtered postings meeting a per-posting skill target (60% by default) by role. Add one skill to the selected set. Use Try one skill to compare newly covered postings with those moving closer. Change the target from 60% to 80% and explain why the counts change. Postings without skills are unscored. Choices stay in the browser and are not sent to a server.

## 3:55-4:35 - Explain recommendations
Read missing-skill recommendations. They rank by additional postings reaching the target, then progress on unmet postings and company breadth. Compare the newly covered count with the separate count that moves closer. Open the small suggested learning project template and explain that it is a preparation prompt, not a promise that the skill is required or that the project proves proficiency.

## 4:35-5:00 - Close with Job postings
Open Job postings. Point to the full posting reference list and its experience, skills, direction, location, and source fields, then use the compact Project files footer for CSV downloads, assignment materials, official provenance, and the one-page methodology. Close with the limits: non-representative ATS sample, unknown skill is not absence, and experience bucket is not graduate eligibility.
